self_assessment: High confidence: located the actual bug (the except-branch in CommonExtras.update_work_ids_individually that deleted the conflicting row after a failed UPDATE), removed the destructive DELETE entirely in favor of a rollback + failed_deletes counter, changed update_work_id to return the required rows_changed/rows_deleted/failed_deletes dict, updated the one internal caller (admin/code.py) that relied on the old tuple-via-list() shape, and verified directly against both a bookshelves_books and a booknotes in-memory sqlite table that on conflict the table is byte-for-byte unchanged and the result dict is exactly {rows_changed:0, rows_deleted:0, failed_deletes:1}; could not run the full pytest suite via conftest.py due to heavy unrelated dependencies (lxml/memcache build failures) so I validated with standalone scripts exercising the same code paths instead, and also updated the one pre-existing test that asserted the old buggy delete-on-conflict behavior.
